result.title: Measuring the Reasoning-Action Coupling in Driving Vision-Language-Action Models through Counterfactuals
result.summary: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models bring an appealing form of explainability to a safety-critical domain, since a system that can state the reasons for its maneuvers offers the transparency that deployment and public trust in autonomous driving demand. These models read the world into language before they act on it, describing the scene and reasoning over it in text that ranges from chain-of-thought to multi-stage question answering on the way to a trajectory. That framing quietly assumes two separable properties, namely that the trajectory follows the generated reasoning and that the generated reasoning tracks the causes that actually produce the trajectory. To thoroughly investigate these properties, we apply causal, counterfactual interventions to four driving VLAs across different benchmarks. First, we perturb the models' own reasoning and show that altering its meaning produces small trajectory changes relative to blanking the same models' camera inputs, a pattern that persists across benchmarks and model architectures. We then construct scene-level counterfactuals through photorealistic removal of key objects named in the models' reasoning and analyze whether the generated reasoning and trajectories track these changes. Overall, our findings indicate that the reasoning these models present to account for their resulting driving behavior is weakly coupled to that behavior itself, pointing to limits on the explainability these systems are intended to provide.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在四个驾驶 VLA 与多个基准上用反事实干预检验推理与动作的耦合：既扰动模型自生成推理的语义，也逼真移除推理中点名的关键物体，观察轨迹是否随之改变。
AI.relevance_reason: 其结论是推理对轨迹的影响弱于遮挡相机输入，直接对应 LVR 关注的「推理内容是否真正被下游使用、贡献如何分配」，这种反事实因果诊断可供核查并可能迁移到 latent 状态的利用率评价。
